The editorial notes Xi's pledge to provide its super-large open market and broad development prospects, describing China as one of the world's largest consumer markets and an indispensable node in many supply chains. It cites figures from the just-concluded China International Import Expo (CIIE), which attracted a record 4,142 exhibitors with intended deals reaching $85.45 billion, while noting China has remained the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years and imported more than 90 trillion yuan ($13.4 trillion) worth of goods between 2021 and 2025. The piece emphasizes that investors judge markets by development prospects as well as size, so Xi's stress on innovation-driven growth was central; he urged deeper cooperation in science and technology, the digital economy and artificial intelligence alongside a green low-carbon transition. It describes China converting robots, autonomous driving and drone food delivery into momentum for high-quality development, and details Xi's pledge to accelerate building a modern industrial system by integrating scientific with industrial innovation, upgrading traditional industries, expanding emerging industries and planning future ones. The editorial also highlights commitments to reduce tariffs, expand market access, explore deeper reforms in rules administration and standards, fully implement both market access and operational access in manufacturing, and steadily expand openness in the services sector. It concludes that Xi's vision of an Asia-Pacific community prospering together offers an alternative to bloc politics, giving smaller and middle powers cooperation rather than pressure to choose sides, framing China's commitment as a durable economic policy grounded in open markets, technological exchange and peaceful coexistence.
items.title: Xi's APEC address framed as defense of openness amid rivalry

items.summary: CGTN's Tian Wei explores how China and the United States can pursue healthy competition while expanding cooperation to make artificial intelligence safer and its benefits more widely shared. As AI agents gain greater autonomy to make decisions and take actions, new risks are emerging, including systems escaping digital sandboxes and acting beyond authorized limits. The two countries are both described as AI powerhouses with distinct strengths: the United States is associated with frontier innovation from Silicon Valley, while China brings computing and energy infrastructure exemplified by Ulanqab. These complementary capabilities carry shared responsibilities for managing AI's risks and distributing its benefits.
items.title: China-US AI Cooperation and Safety Dialogue

items.summary: On Wednesday, Alexander Rossnagel, data protection commissioner for Hesse, announced that his office has opened an investigation into Deutsche Bank following a massive leak of more than 15 million internal records. The probe concerns possible violations of data protection law and will examine whether the bank had adequate protective measures in place and whether it reported the breach to affected individuals promptly, according to Rossnagel's statement: "I am investigating whether Deutsche Bank promptly notified the affected individuals." The leak was carried out by whistleblowers who shared internal documents with a group of international media outlets. Those documents reportedly revealed that the bank had ignored repeated internal warnings about money laundering, corruption and sanctions violations, and named clients including Russian oligarchs, US President Donald Trump, and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. In response to the revelations, Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing acknowledged mistakes in an interview with Handelsblatt, stating: "When you look at the events today, you naturally question whether something could have been done differently." He added that reviewing past decisions might reveal points where priorities could have shifted, while denying that he sought to overlook risks and explaining his reasoning for streamlining customer review processes. The bank said it had reinforced its controls after these matters "date back many years," but the leak has damaged its reputation and pushed its share price down. Deutsche Bank maintains that it proactively informed the relevant authorities about the breach, claims testing found no access to account information, login credentials or payment data, and noted that although the probe will not examine the leaked documents themselves, it will assess the technical and organisational measures in place to determine whether they were appropriate.
items.title: German regulator probes Deutsche Bank over 15 million-file leak

items.summary: On Wednesday, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela during an unexpected visit to Caracas, according to state television reporting. He was received by interim leader Delcy Rodríguez ahead of a planned trip to Colombia later that same day, where he intends to discuss bilateral security cooperation. Framing the deal as a renewal of defence partnership and an opportunity for the two nations' armed forces to work together, Hegseth's remarks were broadcast via footage from VTV, Venezuela's state television channel. The visit had not been publicly announced by the Pentagon beforehand. This move represents another step in the rapprochement between Washington and Caracas that followed Nicolás Maduro's capture in January. The agreement resumes technical and military cooperation between the two countries after years of suspension amid deteriorating diplomatic relations. Rodríguez stated that a primary objective is strengthening Venezuelan armed forces personnel through joint training programmes, which she said would improve preparedness to respond to shared threats. The deal also aims to enhance operational equipment for Venezuelan forces and provide access to new technologies. Neither government has yet disclosed details on the implementation timeline, resources involved, or specific mechanisms of cooperation. Rodríguez assumed power after Maduro's capture, though her continued leadership remains uncertain as her interim mandate expired in July with no announced date for the next presidential election. The broader Washington-Caracas rapprochement has also included agreements over Venezuelan oil and a US strategy against drug trafficking in the Caribbean and Pacific, which has caused at least 240 deaths since September 2025 in attacks on vessels suspected of carrying drugs. Hegseth's visit is part of efforts by Donald Trump's administration to expand its influence in Venezuela; he was the third member of Trump's cabinet to travel there this year, following trips by the interior and energy secretaries focused on Venezuela's oil and mineral resources.
items.title: US Defence Secretary Announces Military Cooperation with Venezuela in Surprise Caracas Visit

items.summary: On Wednesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made a stop in Caracas to announce an agreement deepening defense cooperation with Venezuela. The visit followed the U.S. military operation 10 months earlier that bombed Venezuelan territory and removed Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores from power before transferring them to prison in New York. Hegseth, who will travel to Colombia later Wednesday before continuing on to Ecuador, framed the agreement as ensuring Venezuelans are not threatened by foreign actors, narco-terrorists, or criminals. He delivered remarks from a standing microphone beside acting President Delcy Rodríguez, saying both nations look forward to unlocking Venezuela's prosperity and stability for a safer hemisphere and America. Hegseth noted that Venezuela could draw on U.S. military experience to strengthen security within its sovereign borders. The visit came with little advance notice and limited media presence after Hegseth stopped at U.S. Southern Command headquarters in Doral, Florida. Rodríguez received him hours after returning from a Middle East tour of Turkey, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates. She was accompanied by Defense Minister Gustavo González López, Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco, and businessman Alejandro Betancourt of NABEP, described as a key figure in oil agreements Venezuela has signed with the United States through a Pentagon office. Military and counternarcotics cooperation between Caracas and Washington had been severed in 2005 during Hugo Chávez's presidency. Chávez ended a relationship that included military technology sharing and joint defense exercises, after which Venezuela turned to Russia, Iran, and China as its main suppliers of military equipment. Hegseth is the highest-ranking Pentagon official to visit Venezuela since the operation removed Maduro from power earlier this year, though several senior Defense Department officials have already made repeated trips. These include General Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff who commanded Operation Absolute Resolution on January 3; Southern Command chief Francis Donovan, who oversaw warship and aircraft deployments off the Venezuelan coast as well as strikes against boats allegedly carrying narcotics before U.S. personnel entered Venezuelan territory; Deputy Undersecretary Joseph Humire, who visited in February; and CIA Director John Ratcliffe. The cooperation being formalized has not been limited to official visits but has been underway for months. At least two military and law-enforcement operations carried out in Venezuela over the past year were supported by the United States through equipment and intelligence-sharing. In June, authorities launched an operation against the hideout of Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, known as Niño Guerrero, leader of the Tren de Aragua criminal organization designated a terrorist group by Washington, in the gold-mining region of southern Bolívar State. More recently, drones were used to destroy an operations center belonging to the National Liberation Army guerrilla group in Apure State. In both cases, questions remain about the number and identities of those killed.
items.title: Hegseth Announces U.S.-Venezuela Defense Cooperation Agreement

items.summary:
On Monday night, Ukraine launched back-to-back drone and cruise missile strikes on the Kerch Strait Bridge that links annexed Crimea to Russia's mainland. The first wave left one of the bridge's twin arches slumping sideways; the second brought that arch and a stretch of highway crashing into the sea below. The rail section running parallel to the road remains operational, though passengers captured footage showing a gap where the roadway once stood, with tangled concrete and reinforced steel now lying in the water beneath a shipping route between Russia's Sea of Azov and Black Sea holdings.

The attack was described as the fourth against the bridge since 2022. In October 2022, a truck bomb killed five people including the driver and brought several spans down. In July 2023, Ukrainian naval drones struck it, killing a Russian family visiting from Belgorod. In June 2025, Ukraine said it had launched an underwater attack on the bridge's supports; Russia claimed no damage.

President Volodymyr Zelensky framed the strikes as the final step of a seven-stage operation that gradually degraded Russian radar, air defence and electronic jamming to expose the bridge. He announced the attacks via social media with the message "War will always return to where it began," timed for Wednesday's three-way meeting between Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Natia Seskuria of the Royal United Services Institute noted that Moscow has long used the bridge to move personnel, fuel, equipment and ammunition into southern Ukraine. However, after Russian forces seized a land corridor linking Crimea to Russia's Rostov region at the mouth of the Don River, dependence on the bridge declined though it was not eliminated. Seskuria said the damage reduces flexibility by removing one route for redistributing traffic but does not cut off Crimea or sever supply lines.

The bridge remains important as an everyday transport link connecting Crimean residents with Russia; over summer fuel restrictions were imposed amid strikes on oil depots, tankers and transport facilities. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov downplayed the attacks, saying "There is no doubt that the bridge will be restored - and will be even better than it was before."
items.title: Ukraine strikes Kerch Strait Bridge, damaging road section

items.summary:
Anthropic PBC is set to become the first frontier AI lab to go public, debuting Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. The company priced its shares at $83 each on Wednesday, giving it a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation, about $100 billion above the high end of its previous range. Bloomberg estimates indicate that several financial firms stand to gain billions from the offering.

Iconiq funneled more than $6 billion into Anthropic and holds the largest private investment in its history; based on pre-IPO investments, its stake would be worth over $26 billion at the IPO valuation. Spark Capital invested $75 million in 2023, marking its largest check ever, with a current stake valued at about $11 billion. Menlo Ventures led Anthropic's Series D round with a $500 million check and has invested north of $1 billion total, holding a stake worth nearly $22 billion.

Guy Oseary and Ashton Kutcher wrote an early $35 million check before adding another $400 million; together with Sound Ventures' Effie Epstein, they hold a stake worth nearly $11 billion. Coatue Management invested three times for a total of $4.75 billion, including $2.5 billion in the February round as its largest single private company investment at the time, yielding a stake valued at about $16 billion. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC has invested north of $4.5 billion across Anthropic's last three rounds and holds a stake worth about $15 billion.

Bessemer Venture Partners invested over $800 million for around 0.5% ownership, or about $7.5 billion at the IPO price, representing more than ninefold growth from its initial investment. Lightspeed put more than $3.5 billion into Anthropic starting in early 2024 and planned further IPO investment; based on private financings alone, its stake is valued at about $28 billion. General Catalyst backed Anthropic across various rounds starting in 2025 with approximately $2 billion, holding a stake worth around $10 billion.

Anthropic's largest stakeholders are by far its Big Tech backers: Amazon.com Inc., Alphabet Inc.'s Google, and Microsoft Corp. all hold stakes worth tens of billions after years of investing and partnering with the lab. Anthropic also arranged a $26 billion private placement for seven tech companies to invest further; after those transactions, Amazon owns nearly 15% of Anthropic's outstanding stock and Google owns about 14%. These four companies have been criticized for creating circular deals in which they are simultaneously investors, customers, and distributors while selling competing AI models. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt invested tens of millions in the company in 2021 when it was valued at just $461 million; at a $1.5 trillion IPO price, his stake is expected to be worth about $15 billion.

The reporting relies on Bloomberg estimates and information from people familiar with details who asked not to be identified discussing private information. Calculations may not account for dilution from the IPO, allocations in pending orders are undisclosed, and all parties either declined or did not respond to comment requests.
items.title: Financial investors' windfalls from Anthropic's record IPO

items.summary: Nvidia delivered strong third-quarter results on Tuesday, posting bumper revenue and earnings alongside sales projections that beat Wall Street estimates. Its shares rose as much as 5% in extended trading. This rebound comes after the company's share price fell nearly 40% from its October 6 record high, wiping roughly $2 trillion off its market capitalization and ending its status as the world's most valuable company. The bulk of that decline occurred before Jensen Huang admitted on November 8 to an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed and alleged Chinese spy, leading to his resignation four days later amid allegations of improper relationships with Nvidia employees. Analysts now point to several reasons investors may reconsider buying the stock, including trust and accountability concerns, board leadership questions, US national security worries tied to external investigations such as a reported probe by the Securities and Exchange Commission, customer financing practices, long-term demand for its chips, and the AI business model itself - all of which predate the scandal. Nvidia's ascent was exceptionally rapid: its share of the S&P 500 rose from 1% in December 2022 to 8.5% by May this year, driven by surging chip demand from hyperscalers and neocloud AI partners that Nvidia has often helped finance. Interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress described a "disciplined" approach on Tuesday's earnings call, saying the company would be selective in capital commitments, investments, and guarantees, though she noted there are no plans to change its backstops for neocloud companies. If that stance shifts, firms like CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, and Applied Digital - whose shares have already fallen steeply recently - could decline further. A Bank for International Settlements report published last month examined this vendor-financing trend, finding that between 2021 and 2025 nearly 30% of all AI firms' investment deals by value involved an AI firm on the other side, while 55% of incoming investments in AI firms came from other AI firms. The authors warned these circular relationships can artificially inflate demand, which could become a problem if revenue growth and real end-user demand slow; the AI flywheel could then reverse, potentially causing significant financial market volatility. They also noted many deals are opaque, complex, and private, making them hard to monitor, with risks amplified by growing use of private credit and special purpose vehicles that can create hidden leverage and interconnected exposures during downturns. The article closes by noting the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has dropped nearly 30% over six weeks, suggesting Nvidia's results were not bright enough to mask deep-rooted concerns about the AI ecosystem.
items.title: Nvidia's Strong Q3 Results Amid Deepening Structural Concerns

items.summary:
A week of widespread technology failures across the United States may trace back to a surge in security patches driven by artificial intelligence, according to officials who briefed members of Congress. The Washington Sun reported that Wall Street executives and NSA representatives told lawmakers these disruptions stemmed from attempts to patch vulnerabilities identified by AI models rather than from cyberattacks; instead, the fixes themselves temporarily overwhelmed the systems they were meant to protect. A congressional official explained that AI is identifying massive vulnerabilities so quickly it increases urgency to patch immediately, with organizations pushing through many patches at once in ways exceeding what their systems can handle.

The underlying logic is that companies and government agencies have turned powerful AI models on their own networks to find weak spots before attackers do, but since adversaries now have access to similar tools or will soon, the pressure has pushed banks, tech firms, and intelligence agencies to deploy fixes faster than usual. The scale of this activity grew sharply: Microsoft fixed about 1,400 security flaws in a single monthly update last month, a record, compared with roughly 170 a year earlier; The Wall Street Journal tied the jump partly to AI bug-hunting models including Anthropic's Mythos and similar tools from OpenAI. Serious vulnerabilities have since surfaced in PHP, the Linux operating system, and Java.

The NSA provided the clearest illustration: its classified NSANet network went offline on Tuesday after a software patch for major PHP flaws discovered last month. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the outage was not a cyberattack or coordinated nation-state action but rather many people patching their systems at once, noting that employees were told to stagger arrivals and that the network had been unstable for weeks.

Not every failure fit this pattern. Microsoft's Outlook outage on Thursday affected more than 450 million users over nearly 24 hours and was traced to a latent bug in networking gateway servers dating back to July; The Wall Street Journal reported it separately from the AI patching narrative. The FAA's nationwide ground stop on Friday followed data flooding its network at about 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, with a new router at an El Dorado, Arkansas site among suspects; roughly 3,500 planes landed safely while airlines cancelled around 12,462 flights that day. Chase reported on Monday that a software bug slowed transactions and spilled over to other banks and Zelle payments.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has asked the administration to brief Congress, and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officials are pushing new technology onto old computer systems in ways that overwhelm them, warning that more such incidents will likely occur as new technology rolls out. The Washington Sun cited three sources familiar with private conversations for its reporting.
items.title: US Officials Attribute Tech Outages to AI-Driven Security Patching

items.summary: Nvidia executive Jay Puri has become personally entangled in an unfolding scandal involving his wife, Cenly Chen, a former senior executive of Super Micro Computer (Supermicro). US prosecutors have charged Supermicro executives with conspiring to smuggle $2.5 billion worth of servers containing Nvidia chips to Chinese customers. The Information reported Wednesday that Puri and Chen had told colleagues about their marriage this year, noting that Chen was part of the team managing Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia, though the company has disputed her alleged role in chip allocations. This development follows a report Tuesday by Muddy Waters Research, an influential short-selling firm founded in 2010 by American investor Carson Block, which disclosed it was shorting Nvidia shares and raised questions about Puri-Chen ties. The firm's report, titled NVIDIA: More China, cited photographs from 2024 to 2026 showing Puri alongside a woman identified variously as Cenly Chen and Cenly Puri. It referenced an October shareholder lawsuit alleging that Chen had managed Supermicro's acquisition of GPU chips from Nvidia and decided how to distribute NVDA GPUs among the company's customers, asserting there was no way she lacked knowledge of its illicit sales. At Nvidia, Puri became executive vice-president of Worldwide Field Operations in 2009, overseeing global sales, business development, partnerships and customer relationships; he announced his retirement from that operational role in June but continues as a senior adviser, though reports indicate an uneasy relationship with the company. According to media reports citing insiders, Jensen Huang reportedly berated Puri during a closed-door meeting attended by more than 30 executives in February, telling him he hoped Puri would get the flu and die before adding that his death would put them all out of their misery; Puri reportedly remained silent. Muddy Waters made its reputation investigating Chinese companies listed in Western markets, notably exposing alleged accounting fraud at Sino-Forest, and publishes investigative reports while taking positions in scrutinized shares, giving it a financial interest in Nvidia's share price declining here. The controversy unfolds against an increasingly charged American political climate marked by suspicion of foreign connections, particularly Chinese ones, even as Silicon Valley remains built on international talent, with Indian-origin executives including Satya Nadella of Microsoft, Sundar Pichai of Alphabet and Arvind Krishna of IBM leading some of America's most powerful corporations. Nvidia's crisis has also escalated sharply, with chairman Harvey Jones delivering a decisive rebuff to growing pressure to bring back Huang as CEO, saying the board had unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him; Huang is expected to face congressional questioning on December 1.
items.title: Jay Puri's Ties to Supermicro Exec Amid Nvidia Scandal

items.summary:
Bharatiya Janata Party leader Tejasvi Surya stated that Grand Theft Auto VI has a significant India connection, with much of its development carried out by Rockstar India's studio in Bengaluru. In an X post, he noted that more than 1,600 developers at the Bengaluru studio had worked on the game and described it as one of the most awaited games worldwide. Surya also traced the studio's origins to Dhruva Interactive, which was founded by Rajesh Rao in Bengaluru in 1995 with a single computer. He called this company India's first game development studio and said it was acquired by Rockstar Games in 2019. Surya observed that while Bengaluru is widely recognised for its IT industry, the city's gaming ecosystem represents another facet of its technology sector.

The article provides background on why GTA remains a major franchise, reporting through AP that publisher Take-Two Interactive says the Grand Theft Auto series has sold more than 470 million units worldwide. The series began in 1997 with a top-down game and evolved into an open-world crime franchise despite repeated controversies. Its previous main instalment, Grand Theft Auto V, released in 2013 and accounts for more than 230 million of those sales; the article also states that this game generated $1 billion in retail sales within its first three days of release.

Regarding what to expect from GTA 6, the piece reports it follows a 13-year gap since the previous main instalment. The game is set to return players to Vice City, the franchise's fictional setting inspired by Miami, and features two protagonists while continuing the open-world crime narrative. It has received eight nominations at the 2026 Game Awards, including Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Action/Adventure and Best Performance. The awards ceremony is scheduled to take place on December 10.
items.title: BJP leader Tejasvi Surya credits Bengaluru studio for GTA 6 development

items.summary: According to National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates for 2023-24, government health expenditure per person varies sharply across Indian regions. The four poorer northern states of Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand averaged around Rs 1,651 in per capita spending, which is less than half the Rs 3,501 recorded for the northeastern states and nearly a fourth of the Rs 7,209 average for union territories. Senior Assistant Editor Anuja Jaiswal at The Times of India noted that fixed costs such as capital investment and infrastructure remain relatively high even when the number of people using those services is limited.
items.title: Regional healthcare spending gaps in India

items.summary: The Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) public issue opened on November 19, 2026, and remains open until November 23, 2026. The book-built offer comprises 66.18 crore equity shares and is entirely an offer for sale by existing shareholders, meaning the company will receive no proceeds while all funds go to selling shareholders. The basis of allotment was expected to be finalised on November 25, 2026, with tentative listing on BSE and NSE scheduled for November 27. MCL set a price band of Rs 129-136 per share (face value Rs 2), corresponding to 64.50 times the face value at the floor and 68 times at the upper end. The lot size is 110 shares, with retail investors needing Rs 14,960 to bid one lot at the top of the band. Grey market sentiment was modest: a premium of around Rs 3 per share (nearly 2% over the Rs 136 upper price band) implied an estimated listing price near Rs 139 and a potential gain of about 2.2%, though such premiums are unofficial indicators that do not guarantee returns. Brokerage firm Anand Rathi rated the issue 'Subscribe - Long Term', citing MCL's status as India's largest single coal producer, strong profitability, substantial reserves, mechanised opencast operations, integrated rail and port evacuation infrastructure, long-term Fuel Supply Agreements, and backing from parent Coal India Ltd. The company reported its highest profit after tax among Coal India's listed subsidiaries in FY26, with an operating EBITDA margin of 41.7% and return on net worth of 53.8%. At the upper price band, MCL was valued at 8.4 times its FY26 P/E and 5.9 times FY26 EV/EBITDA, implying a post-issue market capitalisation of Rs 9,00,097 million. On financials, total income rose 3% year-on-year to Rs 33,899 crore in FY26 from Rs 33,029 crore in FY25, while profit after tax declined 1% to Rs 10,698 crore from Rs 10,825 crore. Incorporated in April 1992 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Ltd, MCL operates primarily in non-coking coal across Odisha's Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields, with customers spanning power generation plus cement, steel, aluminium, sponge iron and paper sectors. As of June 30, 2026, it operated 17 mines (14 opencast and three underground) and runs the 10-million-tonne-per-annum Ib Valley Coal Washery; as of September 30, 2026, it employed 20,526 permanent staff. Anand Rathi flagged risks including concentration in non-coking coal, heavy dependence on thermal power sector and government-owned utilities, customer and contractor concentration, regulatory and environmental challenges, and the gradual shift toward renewable energy. The article's brokerage views are attributed to an SEBI-registered research analyst and are not those of The Economic Times Digital.
items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO opens for subscription

items.summary: Contracts for the Nasdaq 100 Index rose 0.9% while those for the S&P 500 climbed 0.5%. This followed Anthropic pricing its initial public offering at $83 per share, making it the biggest first-time share sale on record. Asian equities were mixed early in trading: Japan's Nikkei 225 index was little changed, while Australian shares fell more than 1% as commodity prices declined. Copper plunged Wednesday amid a broad selloff as bullish investors exited positions tied to the AI boom; copper dropped 5.7% on the LME to its lowest level since April, and tin shed 5% in London. Gold tumbled over 3% in the prior session to its lowest point in more than a year after Federal Reserve officials argued for additional interest-rate hikes. Anthropic's listing arrives at a pivotal moment for markets, with Nvidia tumbling recently following Jensen Huang's ouster and growing concerns that technology spending may slow; the IPO serves as a test of whether investors will commit fresh capital to the sector amid deteriorating sentiment. Kyle Rodda of Capital.com described it as "a barometer for how bullish the market really is on AI names," while Dilin Wu of Pepperstone noted that successful pricing does not guarantee shares will rise once trading begins. Investors also reviewed minutes from the Fed's October meeting, which indicated nearly all officials agreed they would likely need to raise rates in coming months to return inflation to their 2% target, with two policymakers suggesting an increase exceeding 25 basis points could be warranted in December if incoming data proved unfavorable. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly called for a measured approach and said "we'll have to further tighten interest rates," while Governor Michael Barr stated higher borrowing costs would likely be appropriate.
items.title: Anthropic IPO and Fed tightening expectations weigh on markets amid mixed Asian equities

items.summary: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins is facing mounting scrutiny over his leadership after Cameron Bancroft, banned for nine months in the 2018 'Sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal, broke his silence with a detailed public account. In an explosive column of about 4,497 words published Wednesday, Bancroft called Cummins' repeated denials of knowledge over eight years the "final straw" that prompted him to speak out, while describing himself as relieved and liberated after carrying the burden for so long. He reiterated claims that the wider Australian team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the 2018 South Africa tour, acknowledging David Warner had raised the idea of using sandpaper on Day 2's tea break in Port Elizabeth, with bowling coach David Saker and then head coach Darren Lehmann present. Cummins has maintained his position unchanged since day one, a stance reinforced by manager Neil Maxwell, who urged people to read Pat's interview transcript and noted Bancroft had been through a lot. The controversy intensified calls for an immediate review of Cummins' captaincy from prominent writer Robert Craddock in The Australian, while broader media questioned whether he could continue as Test skipper amid renewed scrutiny. Bancroft's account reopened wounds from the Cape Town Test, where his sandpaper use led to lengthy bans for him, Warner and then-captain Steve Smith, who was also stripped of the captaincy; the scandal resurfaced after Usman Khawaja's autobiography allegations that the wider team knew about the plan. Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg announced an independent forum allowing players to share their accounts but clarified the body is not seeking a perfect truth or reopening the investigation or imposing fresh sanctions, while former opener Warner said he had nothing further to add and pacer Chadd Sayers questioned whether the process would make complete accounts public. With Bancroft now willing to participate in CA's independent process, Sandpapergate has become once again a major issue for Australian cricket, with Cummins' unchanged denial casting an increasingly uncomfortable test on his leadership.
items.title: Bancroft's revelations intensify pressure on Cummins' captaincy

items.summary: The Hindustan Times published a five-minute morning news brief on November 19 covering politics, national and global events, entertainment, and sports. The lead story reported that US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin were set to hold a trilateral meeting on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders' summit in Shenzhen. China stated the three leaders would engage in "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations." A second story detailed the funeral of slain Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat, held around 10pm Wednesday nearly 160km from his family's one-storey house. In keeping with government policy against handing over bodies of slain terrorists to families and preventing public funerals that could glorify militants, Bhat's body was buried in a village in the Bangus valley of Jammu and Kashmir's Kupwara district; his family resides in Khrewan village in Kupwara. The entertainment section reported that Grand Theft Auto VI began rolling out Wednesday evening as the global release concluded an eight-year development saga, with Indian users gaining access at midnight Thursday. According to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, GTA VI had booked about $1.5 billion—roughly ₹14,100 crore—in pre-orders by Wednesday, surpassing Avengers: Endgame's 2019 record of $1.2 billion in its first weekend global opening. The sports section covered Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan, which the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said moved northwards at a speed of 5 kmph over the west-central and adjoining central parts of the south Bay of Bengal during the six hours ending 11.30pm on November 18, with landfall expected near Odisha and Andhra Pradesh on November 20. The brief also reported an India vs New Zealand Test match in Wellington where Jasprit Bumrah took two wickets while Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep each took one; the hosts were reduced to 60/4 at lunch on Day 1, but Henry Nicholls and Rachin Ravindra steadied the innings with a 39-run stand. The document concluded with an editorial statement from the HT News Desk describing its round-the-clock coverage across politics, economy, business, science and technology, environment, law and order, infrastructure, education, climate issues, and geopolitics.
items.title: Hindustan Times morning news brief for November 19

Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata and members of the Tata Group's board are scheduled to visit Air India's headquarters in Gurugram on Thursday, according to people familiar with the matter. The visit is expected to cover both the airline headquarters and its academy, with board members anticipated to review the carrier's performance as it continues posting losses years after the Tata Group acquired it in January 2022. Senior executives attending may include Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran.

Noel Tata was unanimously appointed chairman of Tata Trusts in October 2024, two days after his half-brother Ratan Tata died. The role placed him at the head of the philanthropic institutions that collectively own about 66% of Tata Sons. He has reportedly differed with the Tata Sons board over Chandrasekaran's reappointment for another five-year term, a planned public offering of Tata Sons, and growing losses in new-age businesses including aviation, electric vehicle batteries, digital commerce, and semiconductors.

The visit coincides with Air India's announcement last month that it would establish a full-time team to systematically review expenditure and identify cost-saving opportunities. In his first internal communication to employees seen by Hindustan Times, CEO Tewolde Gebremariam stated in October that cost savings could not be driven by a single team or function but required the active participation of every employee. He emphasized embedding 'a mindset of frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making' alongside operational excellence.

The focus on costs comes amid challenging conditions for airlines, including elevated oil prices amid the West Asia crisis and pressure on fuel bills, margins, and flight routes. Gebremariam announced that a cross-functional Cost Savings Team had been established to systematically review all expenditure across functions, asking employees to extend their 'full support and cooperation' as it works to deliver cost efficiencies organization-wide.
items.title: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata to visit Air India headquarters

items.summary: Odisha has intensified preparations for Severe Cyclone Akvan, which the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast to make landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha by noon on Friday, November 20. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said around 50,000 people had already been evacuated from vulnerable areas as of Wednesday evening, with the largest operation underway in Ganjam district; the state has set a target of zero casualties. According to an IMD update at 11:30 pm on November 18, Akvan was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal about 480 km southeast of Narsapur, 600 km south of Gopalpur and 660 km south of Puri. The storm is expected to move north-northwestwards before crossing the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, packing sustained winds of 90-100 kmph with gusts reaching 110 kmph. Residents from villages in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts are being shifted to cyclone shelters and relief centres; the state has readied 3,000 cyclone shelters of which 448 were already operational, while Rs 20 crore was allotted to 15 districts for relief and rescue operations. The IMD warned of very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall across large parts of southern and coastal Odisha, including Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda districts, with coastal wind speeds expected to reach around 100 kmph. The government ordered the closure of schools in six districts-Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal-from November 19 to 21 as a precautionary measure, while Khurda district's schools would remain shut for two days; leave was suspended for employees, senior bureaucrats were deployed to vulnerable districts, and recruitment examinations scheduled later that week were postponed. Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the state's strategy had to be revised after the cyclone changed course, expanding the threat from southern Odisha to coastal districts as well. Authorities identified 141 landslide-prone locations across the state, particularly in Koraput and Malkangiri, and began relocating residents; Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil directed tourism authorities to implement safety measures for visitors amid forecasts of rough seas, strong winds and coastal inundation. The Puri Jagannath temple administration announced closure of Shree Gundicha Temple until November 21, while fishermen were advised not to venture into the sea. BJD president and former chief minister Naveen Patnaik urged people to remain alert and cooperate with the administration; he recalled Cyclone Arnab's devastation last month, noting that Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts were still recovering from damage caused by Arnab. Patnaik criticised the BJP government over its handling of the Ganjam floods, describing them as man-made and demanding accountability, while BJD legislators disrupted Assembly proceedings seeking a discussion on flood management and disaster response; Cyclone Arnab's aftermath had left at least 11 people dead and six others missing in Odisha. The IMD forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across parts of southern West Bengal between November 19 and 21, affecting Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, South 24-Parganas, Howrah, Jhargram and Bankura districts; Kolkata was expected to experience thunderstorms and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph. Officials said the cyclone could affect a broad stretch of coastline because of signs of possible recurvature in its track.
items.title: Odisha intensifies evacuations as Cyclone Akvan alters course toward landfall

items.summary:
A new study released Wednesday by the Pew Research Centre, reported through PTI from Washington on November 19, projects that Islam will surpass Christianity to become the world's largest religion by 2035. According to the projections, if current trends continue there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under three billion Christians worldwide by 2070. The study attributes most of this growth not to adult conversion but to births into each religious group. During 2020-2025, Pew reported a fertility rate for Muslims of 3.1 children per woman, compared with 2.5 for Christians and 1.6 for all other women, below the 2.1 replacement level needed for each generation to sustain itself.

The world's total population is projected to rise by 29 per cent between 2020 and 2070, with Christians growing by 30 per cent and Muslims by 80 per cent. Hindu numbers are expected to increase globally but decline slightly as a share of the global population: Hindus will grow from 15 per cent in 2020 to 14 per cent in 2070.

The absolute number of Hindus worldwide is projected to rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070, with India's Hindu population increasing by 176 million over the same period. Outside India, much of this growth will come from Pakistan (over five million) and the United States (over four million). Pew projects Hindus comprise 79.4 per cent of India's religious composition in 2020, sliding to 75.8 per cent by 2070, while Muslims rise from 15.2 per cent to 19.6 per cent over the same period even as India's overall fertility rate falls rapidly.

Nepal and India will remain the only two countries with a Hindu majority, and the United States is projected to have the world's fifth-largest Hindu population. Pakistan will hold the largest Muslim population globally, followed by India, Nigeria, and Indonesia, which currently has the most adherents to Islam. Buddhists are expected to shrink both in number and as a share of the global population, partly due to anticipated declines in China, South Korea, and Japan.

Regarding Christianity's geographic shift, more than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa by 2070, with the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassing the United States as having the largest Christian population. The United States will no longer have a Christian majority, though Christians will remain its largest religious group.

The study also notes steady growth among "nones" -- people who are atheist, agnostic or religiously unaffiliated. Excluding China, which has high proportions of nones but faces sharp population decline, Pew projects the ranks of nones elsewhere will grow by more than 180 million by 2070. The nones already form a majority in ten countries including the Czech Republic, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Vietnam, with South Korea, France, and the United Kingdom forecast to join this group by 2070.
items.title: Pew projects Islam overtakes Christianity as world's largest religion by 2035

items.summary: BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran asserted on Wednesday that the traditional Karthigai deepam will certainly be lit atop the disputed deepathoon at the Thiruparankundram hill temple this year, expressing confidence that the Supreme Court would also deliver a verdict in their favour. Speaking to media after paying floral tributes to freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaranar at his memorial on his death anniversary, Nagenthran said all court verdicts delivered so far had favoured lighting the lamp at the deepathoon. He maintained that the lamp should be lit there and expressed confidence it would be done on Thirukarthigai day, November 24. He urged the Tamil Nadu government to respect the high court verdicts still in force and act accordingly, adding that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had responsibility to protect communal harmony and maintain peace. On a separate matter, Nagenthran called for implementation of the 10 per cent reservation under the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) category among open category communities in Tamil Nadu. He said he had raised the demand in the Assembly during the previous government but then chief minister M.K. Stalin had not considered it, pointing out that the EWS quota was being implemented in central government employment, including in the railways, and urging the Chief Minister to take appropriate action.
items.title: Nagenthran Asserts Karthigai Deepam Will Be Lit at Thiruparankundram

items.summary: The team managing Telugu actor T Gopichand has dismissed reports that he would play the antagonist role in Tamil star Suriya's upcoming film, directing Mathimaran Pugazhendhi. The news emerged after Gopichand gained attention for action films such as Yagnam and Loukyam. In an official statement, Team Gopichand called the circulating social media claims completely false and urged all media outlets and handles to refrain from spreading misleading reports. The team emphasized that any future announcements about his projects would be made exclusively through his official social media accounts. Separately, Suriya is reportedly in discussions with filmmakers including Jai Bhim director TJ Gnanavel and DC director Lokesh Kanagaraj, with one project potentially casting him as a doctor; further details on these films remain pending.
items.title: Team Gopichand Denies Reports of Antagonist Role in Suriya Film

items.summary: Union Minister G Kishan Reddy will pay the full Telangana SSC Board examination fees for 4,741 Class 10 students enrolled across 87 government schools within his Secunderabad Parliamentary Constituency. Described as a continuation of an initiative from previous years, the gesture is framed in keeping with the spirit of Antyodaya and aimed at encouraging students to pursue their education and build bright futures. The Minister extended best wishes to all examinees, urging them to approach the exams with confidence and determination. Separately, Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy emphasized that his government prioritizes the welfare of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). During a meeting on Wednesday at the Dr. Marri Chenna Reddy Human Resource Development Institute in Telangana with Chairman Faggan Singh Kulaste and other members of the Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of SCs and STs, Revanth Reddy briefed them that the government is creating opportunities for these communities across education, employment, economics, and politics. He highlighted political representation, including appointments as Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and state cabinet ministers, along with expanded roles in Public Service Commission positions and various state corporations. The Chief Minister also noted that SCs and STs receive priority wherever they meet necessary qualifications and merit, citing allocation of Indiramma housing scheme homes. This article was auto-generated from an agency feed and edited only for its headline by FPJ's editorial team.
items.title: Kishan Reddy to Cover SSC Fees for 4,741 Students in Secunderabad

items.summary: During promotions for Netflix's series Akka, Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte appeared together. In an interview, Radhika discussed a Telugu film in which her character marries her maternal uncle (mama), stating she disliked everything about the movie. When asked by journalist Priyanka Nair, Keerthy explained that marrying one's maternal uncle is part of Tamil and Telugu culture. At a press conference for her upcoming film Sathyavan Savithiri, Keerthy responded to Radhika's remarks when journalists suggested South Indian cinema should address the situation. She said she had already spoken on the matter, noting at first she did not understand what Radhika meant before realizing it concerned culture. When told the practice is Tamil and Telugu rather than Malayalam, Keerthy corrected him, stating that this culture does not exist in Kerala and adding with respect that she would never let down their culture. She clarified that her earlier comments were offered as information. Netizens had speculated Radhika was referring to the 2014 film Legend, in which she starred opposite Nandamuri Balakrishna without naming it or its actor. NBK fans reacted negatively and resurfaced an older interview where Radhika expressed gratitude for being part of Legend. As of reporting, Radhika had not responded to the controversy. Sathyavan Savithiri, also starring Mysskin in the lead role, is scheduled to release on November 20, 2026.
items.title: Keerthy Suresh Defends South Indian Culture After Radhika Apte's Comments

items.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan returned to his residence in Rampur after being released from Dasna District Jail in Ghaziabad on interim bail. The Allahabad High Court granted the relief on Tuesday, observing that the mandatory provisions governing his arrest were prima facie not strictly followed. He addressed the media Wednesday evening and thanked the court for granting him relief, saying his release was a day of celebration for those who believe in constitutional values, justice, and democracy. Khan said he firmly believed the country is independent but the Constitution is not, adding that people must demand the Constitution be freed. Speaking on the political situation, he declared "Chunav nahi hoga, Inquilab hoga" (no elections will happen, revolution will), asserting contests would now be based on issues rather than caste or religion. He defended himself against mafia allegations, noting he opened schools for children and established a university, and questioned why investigating agencies like the ED, CBI, I-T, and Development Authority did not jail educationists such as Madan Mohan Malaviya and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan if they existed in their time. Targeting the BJP, Khan alleged it had suffered election setbacks and claimed its won seats were secured through foul play, citing both Lok Sabha and Vidhan Parishad results. His son Abdullah Azam Khan arrived at Dasna Jail to welcome him along with SP supporters. The money laundering case relates to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, a private university in Rampur founded by Azam Khan in 2006; on October 28 the ED attached its land and building, putting the book value of the property at Rs 426 crore while its estimated current market value was Rs 1,170 crore. The article is directly published from ANI without editing by DNA staff.
items.title: Azam Khan Granted Interim Bail in ED Case

items.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm 'Akvan' is developing over the westcentral Bay of Bengal, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) assessing it as likely to move north-northwestwards and cross the North Andhra Pradesh-Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on Thursday. The IMD estimates maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, with landfall expected on November 20 in that same stretch from Narsapur to Puri. In response, the Odisha government has mandated closure of all government, aided and private schools along with Anganwadi centres across six districts for three days, running from November 19 to November 21. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi stated at a review meeting held in the State Control Room that the state was fully prepared and had begun taking necessary measures. He noted that heavy rainfall is expected across several Odisha districts, with wind speeds averaging around 100 kmph, particularly affecting southern Odisha and the coastal belt extending as far as Balasore—including Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, and Kalahandi—and reported that a Red Warning has been issued for 13 districts. The state government reportedly held discussions with District Collectors on comprehensive management and response strategy. In parallel, Railway authorities rescheduled three trains due to the cyclone: Train No. 18046 Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express was moved from a 08:40 departure at 15:40 hours on November 19; Train No. 12704 Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express shifted its departure to 17:55 hours, up from 15:55 hours the same day; and Train No. 15227 SMVT Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express moved from a 00:30 departure to 08:30 hours on Thursday. The Indian Navy and other agencies are coordinating preparedness measures while authorities monitor the cyclone's movement, though IMD figures represent forecasts rather than confirmed conditions.
items.title: Cyclone Akvan Reshapes Coastal India with School Closures and Train Reschedules

items.summary: BJP ally Sanjay Nishad, Uttar Pradesh Cabinet Minister and chief of the Nishad Party, staged a sit-in in Maharajganj demanding Scheduled Caste (SC) status for the Nishad-Mallah community. The protest unfolded with his supporters after he was attending an event with party workers; he urged them to take to the streets because their reservation demand would not be met without public demonstration. He then led his followers onto the road and sat down in protest, converting the gathering into a demonstration over inclusion in the Scheduled Caste category. Nishad said the sit-in would continue until BJP's Uttar Pradesh president Pankaj Chaudhary secured an assurance from Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the demand. He chose Maharajganj because it is Chaudhary's Lok Sabha constituency, and he argued that the BJP state president's proximity to the Prime Minister makes him well placed to raise the issue directly with Modi before any withdrawal of the protest could be considered. The demonstration occurred even though the Nishad Party remains an ally of the BJP in Uttar Pradesh, where Nishad serves as a Cabinet minister in the Yogi Adityanath government.
items.title: Nishad Party chief protests for SC status

items.summary:
Indian budget airline SpiceJet has received board approval to raise up to ₹5,500 crore as it faces financial and operational difficulties. During a Wednesday meeting, the board approved the fundraising proposal and informed potential investors of ongoing discussions. If successful, the funds would be raised through a combination of equity and other permitted instruments, strengthening the airline's balance sheet while supporting its revival. The board has directed management to complete all necessary processes at the earliest.

The company also reportedly approved increasing its authorised share capital from ₹2,000 crore to ₹7,500 crore, though this requires shareholder and regulatory approval. SpiceJet plans to deploy the funds toward fleet expansion, meeting operational requirements, and rebuilding its network. Chairman and Managing Director Ajay Singh said the fundraising would provide an important opportunity to rebuild the airline and restore its brand.

The airline is operating in a difficult environment shaped by geopolitical tensions and airspace restrictions affecting nearly all operations, alongside steep increases in aviation turbine fuel prices that have added pressure on costs. SpiceJet has also been losing ground in India's domestic market: according to DGCA data, its domestic share fell from 1.2% in August to 0.6% in September 2026. The airline continues to struggle with unpaid dues, operational fleet and crew shortages, plus widespread cancellations and delays.

Shares gained 4.95% on Wednesday, closing at ₹9.97 on the BSE after the announcement of the proposed fundraising.
items.title: SpiceJet board approves ₹5,500 crore fundraising amid crisis

items.summary:
The Board of Peace, chaired by President Donald Trump and established under his administration, issued its second report to the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday. The board warned that the fragile Gaza peace deal could collapse if Israel and Hamas fail to recommit to pledges made during negotiations. According to a Bloomberg News review of the document, first reported by the Associated Press, the board stated the Gaza peace process cannot advance until an International Stabilization Force deploys in the enclave, Israel fulfills its commitments, and Iran-backed Hamas militants surrender their weapons. The report quoted the board as saying that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely,” adding that if it collapses there would be no Roadmap to return to, no administration to deploy, and no enabling environment to rebuild.

The assessment follows months of intermittent clashes, Israeli airstrikes, and a deteriorating humanitarian situation in Gaza. The board described progress as “limited” and “imperfect,” noting the Palestinian population faces another winter living in tents and rubble. It called on Israel to admit more aid into Gaza, urged both parties to demilitarize, and requested greater UN support.

The report comes a year after the Security Council approved Trump's Gaza plan, though many steps from that original agreement remain unmet: the Palestinian committee meant to govern Gaza has not entered the territory, and an international security force intended to police Gaza and oversee its demilitarization has not deployed. The UN said on Tuesday that already dire living conditions for Palestinians were worsening amid winter flooding.

Violence continued during this period; the UN human rights office reported Israeli strikes had killed more than 1,600 Palestinians since the ceasefire was announced, citing Gaza health ministry data. Funding also remained insufficient, with the UN humanitarian aid appeal only about 40% funded. The board noted that Israeli restrictions on supplies and equipment into Gaza hampered winter preparations, though Israel cited concerns over Hamas diverting dual-use items for military purposes as its reason for limiting critical materials.
items.title: Trump's Board of Peace Warns Gaza Ceasefire Could Collapse
